method.coldOpening: Played cold at 390x844 with Chromium touch emulation (Playwright touchscreen taps and CDP touch swipes) before reading NOTES.md, tools docs or source. First impressions were recorded on nights 1-3 before any source or technical result was opened.
method.run1: Full 30-night run to settlement through visible controls at normal animation speed (no FAST). Final fortune 777,037, rank Harbor Magnate, ledger #1, persisted across reload. Every trade, route, event and finance choice was mine; scratch helper functions only executed the tap sequences (open sheet, set quantity, confirm, select port, Sail) and read back visible text.
method.run2: Fresh second run, contrasting opening, played the same way through night 10 (net worth 34.4k).
method.desktop: 1280x800 Chromium context, keyboard and mouse. Trade, route selection and an event were reached by real key presses and clicks. The settlement screen was reached by keyboard from a labelled fixture (save edited to day 29, one keyboard voyage to night 30).
scriptedChoices: Desktop event hunt: a script alternated number keys 1 and 4 to sail until an event appeared; those destinations were not reasoned choices.
Phone event-contrast audit in run 2 after night 10: a script alternated Lanternquay and Drowned Exchange until a choice card appeared.
Delivery probes (sandbox, denied, corrupt storage) and the pacing probe used a fixed scripted opening: first priced row, default quantity, sail to Drowned Exchange.
Run 1 encounter on night 16: after my first Run choice failed, a loop repeated Run until the encounter resolved (my stated choice each round).
method.supportingHelpers: Frozen repository helpers run against the frozen file after the cold opening, output to scratch only: verify.cjs (8 checks pass, including WebKit touch at 390x844, 390x664, 360x640, 430x932, desktop 1280x800, two full games plus ledger, corrupt storage and restricted sandbox), event-check.cjs 16/16, pr-check.cjs 30/30, trading-check.cjs 14 named checks pass, touch-play.cjs seed 43 (30 nights, settled, WebKit), keyboard-play.cjs seed 31 (30 nights, settled, 0 pointer events).
method.simulation: Repository simulator tools/sim/sim.js driving the frozen file, 13 policies x 40 matched seeds (700000-700039, my seed choice), scratch output. Labelled as simulation; used only to test shortcut claims.

evidence: All logged turns above had a credible runner-up, including the closing turn on night 29.
Cash changed the answer: night 16 the purse left after a full buy disabled the bribe; night 1 and night 7 the reserve line moved me from Max to one unit fewer.

Capacity changed the answer: 70 hold made 40-slot freight nearly free beside depth-limited silk and ink (nights 15, 21, 29); in run 2 a 30 hold filled with pearls while 22k sat idle (night 8), and a full hold cut the escape chance to 18%.
Order size is priced on the sheet: '8 chips avg 7,180, the last at 8,790' (night 11), eels 20 at avg 1,995 with the last at 3,585 (night 26).
Deadline changed the answer on nights 27-29 (fleet windows, freight due night 30, half-price cargo).
1.counterevidence: From about night 10 the high-value goods trade only 3-7 units at the posted price, so hold space rarely binds outside freight and the cheap goods stop mattering. The Compare/Carry strip usually names the best plan and the default quantity is usually right, so many turns were confirmations.

evidence: Map route card gives nights, risk n/5, the toll for the current purse and hold, the cargo quote with its age, and a lower-price test (20% tonight, 25% at 1n, 35% at 2n).
Observation vs arrival before the wireless: rain 174 tonight -> 180; pearls 588 -> 601 at 2n old; Dreamsilk 11,052 -> 8,976 at 3n old; chips 18.3k stale vs 12.9k live the same night.
Flags held: pearls 961 'surge may fade', kelp 186 -> 96, Dreamsilk 30.1k -> 13,572. Fleet estimates: 672 est -> 611; 14.7k -> 17,336.
Rumour confidence matched outcomes: 'sure' landed; 'likely' landed once, landed weak once ('smaller than rumoured'), was unusable once (two nights away), and Pell's tip reversed once.
Run 2 without the wireless: a 1n-old Sluices Dreamsilk quote of 17,098 arrived at 9,221.
2.counterevidence: Glut-priced remote quotes carry no fade flag in the port-quote list (Exchange Moon Ink 8,032 on night 21 was 18,816 on arrival), unlike surges. Unflagged elevated Lanternquay ink quotes fell about 22% on arrival three times. The Exchange route card on night 28 showed services instead of the cargo quote.

evidence: Information: wireless (6,000, night 7) reversed a trade the same night. Capacity: racks 30->45->70 (2,500 and 7,500) made freight compatible with trading. Safety: vault deposits lowered tolls. Depth: Lanternquay charter (20,000) saved 14,090 on its first order.
Early competition for funds: run 2 night 7 had glut eels at 604, the 2,500 racks and 4,463 of 6% debt competing for 9.5k; run 1 night 7 had the wireless against a fifth Dreamsilk.
Liquidity cost of the vault: on nights 15-16 the cash was banked two ports away from a Moon Ink glut.
Shortcut check, direct play: whispers gave +29k by night 6, then a weak one, then one two nights away for a 2,360 fee that scales with wealth.

Shortcut check, simulation (40 matched seeds): informed median 662.6k; stay-whisper 632.5k, ahead in 27.5% of seeds; whisper-spam 298.5k; borrow-max 638.8k; vault-everything 627.3k; round-trip and tally-cornering probes never ahead; no-charter 559.9k; charter-rush 576.4k; greedy 59.0k.
3.counterevidence: Boatyard prices do not scale: racks, motor and a 490 repair were bought without thought from an 84k purse on night 10, and debt cost 3,565 in a 777k run. The charter card estimated '+26 tonight, about 770 loads to pay back' when the buy-side saving that night was 14,090. Freight payouts are fixed at 42k.

evidence: Squall: push-through cost 14% and 10% hull inside the stated 6-16%; shelter in run 2 cost exactly one night and no hull.

Patrol: run at 48% escaped; runs at 45% failed for -12% and -16% inside 9-18%; bribes of 7,058 and 3,591 charged exactly; fight in run 2 missed (-14%), then sank one boat (-12%) and the odds and bribe updated.
Gull Gang: tolls 13,392, 12,911, 5,488 matched the figure quoted on the trade sheet beforehand; a failed run cost 17% hull and 1 of 10 Dreamsilk, matching 'about 12% of each cargo'.
Leak in run 2: patch 2,016 as quoted on the sheet, or jettison 8 pearls.

Recovery after material hits: hull 62% patched to 75% at the Sluices for 208, with a hint row naming the nearest yard; after losing cargo, hull and 19k on night 24 I paid tolls rather than ran for the rest of the run; a missing Moon Ink buyer at Orchid offered a 60% factor sale or carrying on.
4.counterevidence: Several choices are close to dominated: push through at healthy hull (repair is 16-35 per point against a whole night), flotsam at 80%, the gull bag at 70%, and fighting with the starting weapon. Late in the run paying was always right and encounters came on four of five nights. Sinking, collectors and overdue debt were not reached in direct play; all 520 simulated runs sank 0 times.

evidence: Opening: cash-limited bulk cargo under a night-10 debt deadline. Middle: upgrades, vault, parcel deadline, consignments from night 15. Close: fleet windows on nights 21, 25-28 and 29-30, freight due night 30, hull management.
Every one of the 29 turns had a trade, route or finance decision; none passed without one.
Final decision on night 29 was shaped by the deadline (see decision log).

Ending: rank and line, cash + vault + half-price cargo - debt = 777,037, six stats including debt interest 3,565, vault earned 58,769, losses and forfeits 60.0k, and '72,963 short of Sovereign of Gloamwater'. Arithmetic checked.
5.counterevidence: Nights 11-20 mostly repeat one pattern (most discounted high-value good to the best live quote). The settle confirmation says 'plus cargo' without the half-price rule, which is stated in the handbook and on the ending. The ending shows only the next rank, not the ladder.

evidence: Run 2 changed prices and the fleet calendar order (pearls at Orchid nights 1-4, saffron at Lanternquay nights 29-30).
Early plan changed: no cheap rain, so Max pearls to the Exchange, then saffron to Orchid; a courier job on night 3 for 3,540 set the route to the Sluices.

Later plan changed: part-repaid debt on night 4; sheltered and lost a night; bought 14 flood-glut eels at 604 on night 7 (+24,485); followed Pell's tip into a pearl surge at Lanternquay (+21,266); lost on a stale Dreamsilk quote without a wireless.
Net worth at night 10 was 34.4k against 83.8k in run 1.
Untried approaches worth a run: wireless before night 5, charter-first at the hub, weapons with fight-for-quiet-nights, heavy freight.
6.counterevidence: Port supply and import roles, goods and the upgrade list are fixed, and most events in run 2 had already appeared in run 1.

evidence: First buy: 'Compare 22 Bottled Rain -> Sluices, 174 each, seen tonight, risk 3/5, at 20% lower +972', sheet prefilled with a 15% reserve and a reserve line.

I played 30 nights without leaving the game for rules; the handbook is one screen.

evidence: Seven districts with distinct inline art and one-line descriptions; named dealers with their own lines (Marrow Quill, Odile, Brother Tallow, Madame Ysolde, Pell, Grandmother Wick, Old Fenna); flavour text on goods.

Sound, judged by instrumenting Web Audio only: context state 'running'; buy starts 2 triangle tones and noise, sell 3 triangle tones, noise and sine tones, voyage 2 noise bursts and 5 sines; source defines 18 named cues plus ambience.
Mute: M key gave 0 audio nodes on the next buy; the header button restored them; the setting is stored.
Pace: buy confirms in about 0.18s; voyage 2.7s, 1.1s with tap-to-skip.
9.counterevidence: The gull-bag result on night 6 showed no card; a market bulletin toast replaced it and the outcome was only in the log. The log calls bonded freight a 'sealed parcel', and an empty search is titled 'Confiscated'. The phone market panel carries no district art, so districts look alike there. Listening quality was not judged.

evidence: Run 1, run 2 and all desktop work: 0 page errors, 0 console errors or warnings, 0 non-file requests.
Persistence: ledger entry survived reload; a mid-run save resumed at the same night, purse and cargo; a reload during a pending event resumed with the outcome already applied.

Delivery probes (mine): file:// boot; iframe sandbox='allow-scripts' where localStorage throws SecurityError, game playable; localStorage getter throwing, playable; garbage in all three keys, playable; a well-formed hostile save (cash 1e12, unknown port, negative hull) discarded; a score name containing an img tag rendered nothing.

Static: one 272,410-byte file, no script or stylesheet sources, no fetch/XHR/WebSocket, only the SVG namespace URL; storage calls wrapped in try/catch with a memory fallback; NOTES.md present at 59 lines.
Frozen helpers all pass (see method).
10.counterevidence: No material defect found. The ledger date is UTC (2026-11-19 against a local 2026-11-18). I saw no notice when a damaged save was discarded, though NOTES.md says one is shown. The save accepts an edited day value. WebKit evidence comes only from the frozen helpers.

requiredChecks.trendVisuals: sparkline per row, 14-night chart and usual-range bar in the sheet

priorities: Make remote price signals symmetric and complete: flag fading gluts and other temporarily elevated quotes the way surges are flagged, show the held cargo's quote on every route card, and let the charter card count buy-side depth savings so its payback estimate is not misleading.

Keep money decisions alive after night 10: scale boatyard and repair prices or add later-tier costs so upgrades and hull damage still compete with cargo, and rework the near-dominated answers (squall at healthy hull, flotsam, gull bag, starter-weapon fights) and the late run of pay-or-lose ambushes.

Fix the interaction gaps found in play: show a result card for the gull-bag outcome, accept tab taps straight after a sheet closes, stop the rank line overlapping the night bar at 390px, keep the cost summary and reserve line visible in the 1280x800 trade sheet, and guard 'Stay the night' against a stray tap.
limits: Touch was emulated in Chromium (Playwright taps, CDP touch swipes). No physical phone, no iOS Safari, no rubber-banding, safe-area or double-tap behaviour was observed; WebKit coverage is from the frozen helpers only.
No audio was heard. Sound was judged by counting and typing the Web Audio nodes each action starts and by reading the synth definitions; loudness, mix and pleasantness are unjudged.
Tap sequences for routine actions were run by scratch helper functions; choices were mine except the scripted items listed under method.
The desktop settlement screen was reached from a labelled save fixture (day set to 29). A full desktop keyboard run is supported only by the frozen keyboard runner.
The second run stopped at night 10 as specified.
Not reached in direct play: sinking, Marrow's collectors, overdue debt at 10%, heavy freight, borrowing more, winning a fight, dock work. Fixture and simulator evidence covers some of these.
Shortcut comparisons use the builder's simulator with 40 seeds per policy; this is a small sample and bots are not players.
Contrast ratios were computed from CSS colours with gradient backgrounds averaged; no screen reader or zoom testing was done.
Chromium only for my own play and probes; one machine, one session.
